analysis: Both changed files are test-only. NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests.swift (head lines 37-39) adds a `.toolCallDelta` case to the exhaustive switch in `trace`. The new case calls XCTFail and returns "D", and the added comment says the Super output holds calls until validation and never streams fragments. This only adjusts the test to an upstream MLXServerGenerationEvent enum that gained a `.toolCallDelta` case. It adds an assertion that streamed tool-call fragments are never emitted before validation, which supports the existing fail-closed tool policy. ProviderLoopStreamChunkTests.swift (patch hunks near lines 59, 282-283, 299 and 312) wraps OpenAIToolCall values in OpenAIToolCallDelta and uses optional chaining on `function`, to match the parser's new delta type. The tests still check that `encodeToolCallsForHash` is deterministic and framed with \u{1F} markers, so the response-hash domain for tool calls is still covered by tests. No production code, crypto, authorization, attestation or cache storage behavior (T-041, TB-007) changes in the supplied evidence. Remaining integration question: the production-side change that introduced OpenAIToolCallDelta, with an optional `function`, and changed `parseStreamChunk` and `encodeToolCallsForHash` is outside this batch. Reviewers of those sources should check that tool-call fragments with nil or partial function fields are still folded correctly into the attested response hash, and that no plaintext leaks on encryption failure (T-008). These tests give no evidence of a regression in either area.
